title: Ayutthaya Kingdom
summary: King Ramathibodi I founded Ayutthaya about 1350 on an island ringed by three rivers that linked it to the sea, and it became the second capital of Siam after Sukhothai. Filling the gap left by the fall of Angkor, it grew into one of the world's largest and most cosmopolitan cities, a centre of diplomacy and trade between East and West, ruled by 34 kings of five dynasties over about 417 years. In 1767 a Burmese army razed and burned the city, which was never rebuilt there.

uncertainty.note: Founded c. 1350 CE (1893 B.E.) by King Ramathibodi I (traditional date 1351); destroyed by the Burmese army in 1767 CE (2310 B.E.).
